        "The complete one-path owned diff and full 154-line owned module were read. This is a separate part2 phase after the seven caller changes in 4298. The integration, trunk and trunk-only predicates now read params[project]; the release predicate calls release_level(params) rather than checking membership in RELEASE_PROJECTS.         "The table is installed into gecko_taskgraph.util.attributes by the module's local patch_attributes function. Both patch functions run at import time. Exact accepted alias/patch/registration objects are retained from B's completed source study with their original timestamps and keys; this does not audit or credit B's 4300 import change.",
        "The newly referenced release_level name has no local definition or import in the complete owned module. This is a source binding gap at part2, not a newly executed NameError. B owns the later import repair; its focused binding lesson is not duplicated here. The helper is evaluated before the toolchains alternative on the right side of or, so that alternative is not evidence the helper is skipped.",
        "The accepted module imports mozilla_taskgraph and calls release_level(PROJECT_RELEASE_BRANCHES, params), unlike the one-argument owned lambda. Its local comment says the duplicated map is used because the target-task filter path has no graph_config. The accepted registration imports the module with a specific F401 explanation, and retained patch code installs RUN_ON_PROJECT_ALIASES. Reuse the existing focused import/registration lesson.",
        "The accepted PROJECT_RELEASE_BRANCHES constant contains only comm-central, comm-beta, comm-release and comm-esr153. The separately inspected accepted taskcluster/config.yml also contains comm-esr140 and enterprise-thunderbird with enterprise-main, enterprise-beta and enterprise-release. Thus the comment's mirror description is not a literal full copy of the configured graph map.",
        "The exact retained accepted env_subst caller passes config.graph_config[release-branches] and params, whereas the alias passes the smaller constant and params. This establishes a static input-map difference. It does not by itself establish which job/project combinations reach these paths, how the unpaired external helper classifies missing projects or any observed release misclassification.",

        "Full primary Bug 2007240 is reused from the same exact C collector capture already reconciled in 4298: all available description, numbered 1–3, activity/footer and actor-based robot exclusion.
